summary: The reader has completed undergraduate computer science: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, basic number theory, finite sets, permutations), linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers (matrices, rank, invertibility, linear maps), and basic algorithm design including recursion, divide and conquer, recurrences, and the standard school and Karatsuba multiplication. They know Turing machines and tapes and probably the FFT as an algorithm, but not abstract algebra beyond basics, finite fields in depth, or any research-level multiplication algorithm.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and residue rings
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo m, with addition and multiplication of residue classes.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a sum of bits times powers of two, and n-bit integers have n such digits.

known.name: Matrices, linear maps and rank
known.gloss: Linear maps are represented by matrices, with rank the dimension of the image and invertibility meaning an inverse map exists.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijective reordering of a finite set of positions.

known.name: Logarithms and exponents
known.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm and powers of two and their logarithms obey the usual identities.

known.name: Recurrences and divide and conquer
known.gloss: Running times of recursive algorithms are described by recurrences solved by unrolling or standard theorems.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform
known.gloss: The O(N log N) divide-and-conquer algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform of length N, built from butterfly steps.

known.name: Karatsuba and schoolbook multiplication
known.gloss: Elementary integer multiplication algorithms taking quadratic and about n^1.585 time respectively.

known.name: Floating-point and rounding errors
known.gloss: Approximate real arithmetic incurs bounded rounding errors that can be added using the triangle inequality, and rounding to the nearest integer recovers an integer when the error is below 1/2.

known.name: Sets, products and tuples
known.gloss: Finite sets, Cartesian products of index ranges, subsets, tuples and lexicographic ordering of tuples.

known.name: Linear-time scanning of tapes
known.gloss: A Turing machine can copy, compare, add and subtract integers by sequential passes over its tapes in linear time.

known.name: Asymptotic constants and small epsilon exponents
known.gloss: Constants independent of n may be absorbed in big-O, and exponents slightly below one distinguish polylogarithmic growth rates.
